Faithful translation of the official easy_drug source restructured in KO — no new medical facts, no weakening of efficacy/contraindications/cautions, pharmacist-consultation routing preserved. b7e84bfad150d52b.title: Histal Tablet
b7e84bfad150d52b.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort, gastric bloating, food stagnation (gastric stasis), nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, acid belching, indigestion, loss of appetite (anorexia), overeating, promotion of digestion, and gastric bloating caused by indigestion.
b7e84bfad150d52b.usage:
Adults: take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times daily after each meal.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
b7e84bfad150d52b.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients on dialysis; patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption; children (under 15 years); pregnant women, women who may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: allergy symptoms to this medicine (rash, redness, itching, etc.); kidney disorder; liver disorder; low phosphate; patients hypersensitive to Yellow No. 4 or with prior experience of it; patients with high blood pressure; the elderly; heart disorder; oedema.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take together with gastrointestinal analgesics or antispasmodics. Consult a pharmacist when taking with potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, glycyrrhizic acid or its salt preparations, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).

If allergy symptoms (rash, itching, etc.), palpitations, drowsiness, vertigo (dizziness), lassitude, headache, constipation, or dry mouth occur, or if urine output decreases, the face or hands and feet swell, the eyelids feel heavy, the hands become stiff, blood pressure rises, or myopathy (weakness, limb cramps, paralysis, etc.) appears, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist. Rarely, palpitations and elevated GOT/GPT may occur.

summaryTable.How it works: Relieves hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort and bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, acid belching, indigestion, and loss of appetite
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort, gastric bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting

bebeb38e1b2b13de.title: Beecom C Power Tablet
bebeb38e1b2b13de.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, D, and E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, reduced physical strength during and after illness, in the growth period, and in old age; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), beriberi and eye strain, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; to relieve pigmentation (melasma, freckles) caused by sunlight and skin conditions; to help prevent bleeding gums and nosebleeds; to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets; and to relieve peripheral circulatory disorder and menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet.
bebeb38e1b2b13de.usage:
Children aged 8 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, twice daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
bebeb38e1b2b13de.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; hypercalcaemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause); kidney disease; infants under 3 months; patients with kidney stones.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: infants under 1 year; children who get a lot of sunlight and eat a normal diet; hyperoxaluria (excessive excretion of oxalate in the urine); pregnant women, women who may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women; premature infants and young children; gout; kidney stones or prior experience of them; patients with a predisposition to thrombosis (blood-vessel blockage). If there is no improvement after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the supervision of a guardian.

This medicine may turn the urine yellow, affecting clinical test values, and may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests.

Do not take together with levodopa. Consult a pharmacist when taking with oral contraceptives containing estrogen.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, gastric discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, loose stools, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating occur, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the amount gradually increases, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, D, and E; relieves neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, stomatitis, and pigmentation; helps prevent bleeding gums and rickets
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, pregnancy/breastfeeding, reduced strength during and after illness, growth period, old-age vitamin supply

c09484d695fa71d2.title: Continforte Tablet
c09484d695fa71d2.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins B1, B2, and B6 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and reduced physical strength during and after illness. Through the vitamins it contains, it is used to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, lower back pain, joint pain such as shoulder stiffness, beriberi, and eye strain.
c09484d695fa71d2.usage:
Adults aged 19 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily after a meal.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
c09484d695fa71d2.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: if there is no improvement after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist; patients deficient in folic acid.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take levodopa while taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, loose stools, diarrhoea, stomatitis, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, constipation, erythema, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or fluid retention in patients with renal or heart failure occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins B1, B2, and B6 and relieves neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, beriberi, and eye strain
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, pregnancy/breastfeeding, reduced strength during and after illness

d1710e8ea554557b.title: Dentigold Capsule
d1710e8ea554557b.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used as adjuvant treatment for gingivitis after periodontal treatment and for mild to moderate periodontitis.
d1710e8ea554557b.usage:
Adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times daily after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
d1710e8ea554557b.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: children under 15 years; patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: people who have experienced allergy symptoms (rash, redness, itching, etc.) from medicines, cosmetics, eggs, etc.; people of allergic constitution. If there is no improvement after 1 month or more of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

If rash, redness, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, gastric discomfort, nausea, vomiting, stomatitis, or symptoms of Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) — such as fever, erythema, itching, eye congestion, stomatitis, a high-fever rash and redness over the skin and the mucous membranes of the mouth and throat, or burn-like blisters and other severe symptoms — appear, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Adjuvant treatment for gingivitis after periodontal treatment and for mild to moderate periodontitis
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Gingivitis after periodontal treatment, mild to moderate periodontitis

d7f61ed1a5341c66.title: Nosid Tablet
d7f61ed1a5341c66.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort, gastric bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and acid belching.
d7f61ed1a5341c66.usage:
Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
d7f61ed1a5341c66.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; patients on dialysis; women within the first 3 months of pregnancy; children under 7 years; hypermagnesaemia; hyperphosphataemia; constipation; intestinal stenosis; acute appendicitis; patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: pregnant women or women who may be pregnant and breastfeeding women; those with hypermagnesaemia or experience of magnesium deficiency; patients with or with experience of kidney disorder. If there is no improvement after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take together with tetracycline antibiotics. Consult a pharmacist when taking with digoxin, captopril, cimetidine, ranitidine, famotidine, theophylline, propranolol, atenolol, ferrous sulphate, chlorpromazine, acetylsalicylic acid, naproxen, metoprolol and levodopa, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, ketodeoxycholic acid, sodium fluoride, isoniazid, enoxacin, norfloxacin, levothyroxine, or coumarin derivatives. Avoid carbonated drinks immediately after taking.

If diarrhoea, constipation, abdominal bloating, skin rash, numbness, phosphate deficiency, or rarely headache, drowsiness, dizziness, or weakness occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist. Accumulation of aluminium in nerve and bone tissue may occur.

summaryTable.How it works: Relieves hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort and bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and acid belching
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Hyperacidity, heartburn, gastric discomfort, gastric bloating, food stagnation, nausea

eebe707f8213e2c3.title: Minesupply Tablet
eebe707f8213e2c3.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin C, zinc, and selenium during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, and reduced physical strength during and after illness.
eebe707f8213e2c3.usage:
Children aged 12 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, twice daily, or 2 tablets at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
eebe707f8213e2c3.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; Wilson's disease; infants under 12 months; patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: hyperoxaluria (excessive excretion of oxalate in the urine); pregnant women or women who may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; premature infants and young children; gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis; heart and circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinaemia; gallbladder-related disease; liver disease; diabetes; gout or kidney stones. If there is no improvement after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests.

Do not take together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist when taking with antialdosterone agents or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, coma, dermatitis, foul odour in sweat and breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorder, digestive disorder, low blood pressure, or pulmonary oedema occurs, consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamin C, zinc, and selenium during fatigue, pregnancy/breastfeeding, and reduced strength during and after illness
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, pregnancy/breastfeeding, reduced strength during and after illness

f0dc37bed8ed92f6.title: Ceretop C Soft Capsule
f0dc37bed8ed92f6.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins A, C, and E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, reduced physical strength during and after illness, and in old age; to relieve eye dryness and night blindness (difficulty seeing at night); to relieve peripheral circulatory disorder and menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet; to relieve pigmentation (melasma, freckles) caused by sunlight and skin conditions; and to help prevent bleeding gums and nosebleeds.
f0dc37bed8ed92f6.usage:
Adults: take 1 capsule at a time, once daily after a meal.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
f0dc37bed8ed92f6.caution:
Warning: taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations. Women within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts; infants under 12 months.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: pregnant women or women who may be pregnant; breastfeeding women; premature infants and young children; hyperoxaluria; gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional (localized) enteritis; heart and circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinaemia; gout or kidney stones; patients with a predisposition to thrombosis (blood-vessel blockage); patients with abnormal fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia, or pancreatitis, or patients requiring caution with lipid emulsions; patients at particular risk from fat overload; patients hypersensitive to Yellow No. 5 or with prior experience of it. If there is no improvement after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests.

Do not take together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids while taking this medicine. Consult a pharmacist when taking with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, antialdosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea during, before, and after taking this medicine.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful joint swelling, gastric discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, redness, dermatitis, foul odour in sweat and breath, hair loss, restlessness occur, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the amount gradually increases, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

f9129458bb5fc2b4.title: Dongsung Jeongrohwan F Pill
f9129458bb5fc2b4.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for diarrhoea, food stagnation, loose stools, and vomiting with diarrhoea.
f9129458bb5fc2b4.usage:
Adults and those aged 15 years and over: take 3 pills at a time. Those aged 11 to under 15 years: take 2 pills at a time. Those aged 8 to under 11 years: take 1 pill at a time. Take 3 times daily after meals.
Allow an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
f9129458bb5fc2b4.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: children under 7 years. Do not take continuously for 1 week or more.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: patients with diarrhoea accompanied by fever; the elderly; patients with bloody stools or persistent mucous stools. If there is no improvement after several days of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the supervision of a guardian.

If, rarely, loss of appetite or gastric discomfort occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.
